clue.text: Obvious one, Mog, more than your typical effort?

blocks.note: overt means open and obvious
the Roman numeral for one
the setter, Mog, refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A cat-named setter boasting of putting in an obviously bigger effort than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for the setter, so Mog gives ME, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is work done beyond normal hours, so it is extra effort beyond the usual amount.

clue.text: Heat-resistant articles are woven differently

indicators.note: differently means arranged another way, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fireproof goods made by weaving in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovenware is cookware such as dishes made to withstand oven heat.

clue.text: Anxious energy to get on rides, at first

indicators.note: at first keeps only the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to get on in years is to age
the opening letter of rides

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about the energy needed to board fairground rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious can mean keen or impatient to do something, as in anxious to please.

clue.text: No red dresses within limits of Tashkent

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept
within places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Tashkent
saris are dresses worn in South Asia

explanation.surface: No red clothes on sale in the Uzbek capital, Tashkent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No red' reads like a colour rule, but it means opposed to the Reds, the Bolsheviks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarist supported Russia's monarchy, so was an opponent of the Red revolutionaries.

clue.text: Giant periodical with dogs between the covers

indicators.note: between the covers means inside the outer letters, so only the middle is kept

blocks.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a periodical
the inner letters of dogs

explanation.surface: A huge magazine with dogs pictured inside its covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants, whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Magog is a giant of British legend, so the name is an example of a giant.

clue.text: Impact little

blocks.note: first meaning: to affect or make contact with
second meaning: a small amount

explanation.walkthrough: Two bare words read like a phrase about a small effect, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch is to affect or strike, and a touch is a slight quantity of something.

clue.text: Trouble near the capital

indicators.note: trouble suggests stirring things up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unrest close to the seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Teheran, an older spelling of Tehran, is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: How pupil ends, limited by the result of zero labour?

definitions.text: How pupil ends, limited by the result of zero labour?

indicators.note: limited by means bounded on both sides, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: what comes without work is unearned
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Wondering how a student turns out when they put in no work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a pupil who does no work ends up knowing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlearned means uneducated or ignorant, the state of a pupil who never studied.

clue.text: Try organ meat, spitting out the tail

indicators.note: spitting out the tail means the final letter is removed

blocks.note: heart is an organ eaten as offal

explanation.surface: Urging someone to taste offal but spit out the gristly end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like an invitation to taste, but it is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who hears a case tries it in court, so hear and try are synonyms here.

clue.text: Architectural feature starting to go green?

blocks.note: first meaning: a decorative strip, as on a cornice
second meaning: becoming covered in fungus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go green' suggests environmental building, but it is food or walls growing fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulding is an ornamental band in architecture, and something moulding is developing green fungal growth.

clue.text: Is it Scotch for one with last of Laphroaig?

indicators.note: last of asks for only the closing letter of the following word

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, for one
the final letter of the whisky's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a drink mixed with Laphroaig, an Islay malt, counts as Scotch whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, given Laphroaig; but the answer is a thing that can be Scotch, as in a Scotch egg, a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is a familiar British snack, so this food is one thing that can be called Scotch.

clue.text: Playing in La Liga, half-hoping for English appreciation?

indicators.note: half means only part of the following word is kept, the rest dropped
playing suggests letters moving about freely in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, then halved to its first three letters

explanation.surface: A footballer in Spain's La Liga hoping for some appreciation back in England.
explanation.walkthrough: La Liga is Spain's top football league; the first half of hoping is HOP, and with IN and LALIGA it is shuffled into ANGLOPHILIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglophilia is a fondness for England and things English, so it is admiration of the English.

clue.text: Reviewed rank with chess piece on

indicators.note: reviewed hints at looking back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or seats
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Someone surveying a rank of pieces with a chess piece placed on a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a position word for the chess piece, but it is the definition, as a machine that is on.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that is on is running or operating, so it is in working order and functioning.

clue.text: Something of a cowboy song lieutenant's adopted

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: An army officer taking up a cowboy ballad as his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, the rope a cowboy carries for catching cattle.

clue.text: Books printed by agent provide new dirt?

blocks.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible's first part

explanation.surface: A literary agent getting books printed that dish new scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirt' sounds like gossip, but it is soil: to repot a plant is to give it fresh compost.
explanation.definitionFit: Repotting moves a plant into a new container with fresh soil, giving it new earth to grow in.

clue.text: Bird crest, bit on its head

blocks.note: a part is a bit
a crest is the ridge of a hill

explanation.surface: A bird with a crest and a scrap of something on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, on its head puts the bit above the crest.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird, famous from the pear tree of the carol.

clue.text: Emotional moment interrupted by short buzzer

indicators.note: short means the following word loses its final letter
a thing interrupted has something placed in its middle

blocks.note: a point is a moment in time, as in at that point
a gnat is a buzzing insect, cut to its first three letters

explanation.surface: A touching scene spoiled when a brief buzzer goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' suggests an alarm or quiz device, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poignant stirs strong feelings of sadness, so it is emotional or moving.

clue.text: Sting reduced concert attendance, raising cost

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short by its last letter
in a down answer raising lifts the word upward, reading it bottom to top

blocks.note: a prick is a sting
the gate is the number of people attending an event

explanation.surface: The singer Sting playing to a smaller crowd and putting his prices up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the musician, but it is a prick; gate is the British term for attendance at a game or show.
explanation.definitionFit: A price tag is the label stating cost, and by extension the cost itself.

clue.text: Pair of chic yellow shades help when solving?

indicators.note: a pair of means two letters, taken from the front of the word

blocks.note: the opening two letters of chic
ambers are yellowish-orange shades

explanation.surface: Stylish yellow sunglasses, worn perhaps while doing a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary many British crossword setters and solvers use.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chambers Dictionary is the standard reference for cryptic solvers, so it helps with solving.

clue.text: Crowing bantam to begin with provocation

indicators.note: to begin with points at only the opening letter of the previous word

blocks.note: the opening letter of bantam
ragging is teasing, a form of provocation

explanation.surface: A bantam cockerel crowing because something provoked it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragging is British for teasing or taunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowing in its figurative sense is boasting loudly, which is bragging.

clue.text: Bit of glory and gold boring dull pope

indicators.note: a bit of the word means just its opening letter
boring means drilling into, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the opening letter of glory
or is gold in heraldry
grey means dull or dreary

explanation.surface: A tedious pontiff, all gold and glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregory is the name of sixteen popes, including Gregory the Great.

clue.text: Harrow, I'd think, is more than enough for range

indicators.note: the phrase holds more letters than needed, so the wanted letters sit inside it

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the school's name, I'd and the start of think

explanation.surface: Musing that a Harrow education would be ample for someone's scope.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, there only for its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Width is extent from side to side, and range likewise means breadth or extent.

clue.text: Document naked twirling at rave

indicators.note: twirling suggests spinning around, so the word faces the other way

blocks.note: raw can mean naked or bare
to rave is to rant

explanation.surface: A naked dancer spinning at a rave, perhaps prompting police paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant is an official document authorising something, such as a search or arrest.

clue.text: Announced imported cheeses move briskly

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: Brie is a French cheese, so imported in Britain

explanation.surface: A shop advertising that its foreign cheeses are selling fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To breeze is to go along in a quick, carefree way, as in breezing into a room.

clue.text: Recalled cunning corporation chasing Swindon's foremost rock band

indicators.note: recalled suggests calling back, so the word runs backwards
foremost takes only the leading letter of the town's name

blocks.note: the opening letter of Swindon
art means cunning or craft, as in artful
corporation is jocular for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A rock band from Swindon, an English town, dropped by a crafty record company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock band' looks musical, but it is a layer of rock; corporation is an old joke word for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a geological layer, a band of rock lying between others.

clue.text: Detect hint of marjoram in stock

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, here the opening letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a shop that stocks something sells it
the opening letter of marjoram

explanation.surface: Picking up a trace of the herb marjoram in a soup stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like the broth, but it is the verb, as a shop stocks goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell something is to detect it by scent.

clue.text: Style, say, with top tucked in

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, and tucking it in moves that letter into the middle

blocks.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: Fashion advice that style means tucking your top in.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a free shuffle: only the leading S moves, slipping in after TA, as a shirt tail is tucked into trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste means good judgment in aesthetic matters, which is style or elegance.

clue.text: Still night before noon?

blocks.note: an eve is the night before an event
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is still night before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before noon' looks like a single phrase, but before belongs with night.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and still are interchangeable intensifiers, as in even better and still better.

clue.text: Come read about cuts by movie's producer?

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned round and moved about into a new order
to cut into something is to sit inside it, splitting it

blocks.note: via means by way of
taken as written, then shuffled

explanation.surface: An invitation to read about cuts made by a film's producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Producer' suggests a film executive, but the thing that produces a home movie is a device.
explanation.definitionFit: A video camera records moving pictures, so it literally produces a movie.

clue.text: Date and make out

blocks.note: first meaning: to go out with someone romantically
second meaning: to discern or perceive

explanation.walkthrough: Date and make out look like a romantic sequence, but make out here means discern.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing someone is having a relationship with them, and to see is also to perceive or discern.

clue.text: Born daddy, never mind the tot clinging

indicators.note: never mind tells us to ignore, and so remove, the named part

blocks.note: née means born, used before a maiden name
taken as written
to tot up is to add, so the letters of add are dropped

explanation.surface: A newborn's father ignoring the toddler hanging on to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler, but it is the verb to tot, meaning add up.
explanation.definitionFit: A needy person is clingy, demanding constant attention and reassurance from others.

clue.text: Lack of verve in Florida, given temperature along cape

blocks.note: FLA is an abbreviation for Florida
T is the abbreviation for temperature
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbours

explanation.surface: A dull spell in Florida's heat along a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatness is dullness or lack of liveliness, as in a flat performance without spirit.
